See the applicable Models at a glance for model-specific endpoint, service-tier, and feature support\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Quota management\\\\n\\\\nCross-Region inference quotas on the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint are measured in tokens per minute (TPM) per model. When your usage exceeds the quotas at peak times, resource throttle can occur even with previously successful batches. To make sure that your application\\'s request volume doesn\\'t exceed the quotas, monitor the\\xa0**InputTokenCount** and **Invocations** [Amazon Bedrock runtime metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring-runtime-metrics.html).\\\\n\\\\nSpecific models have separate quotas for Requests Per Minute (RPM) and Tokens Per Minute (TPM) that Amazon Bedrock enforces concurrently.\\\\n\\\\nNewer model versions can have different quotas than previous versions.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:** The Service Quota dashboard shows only configured quotas, not real-time usage. To monitor real-time usage, use CloudWatch\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Analyze Amazon Bedrock cost spikes with AWS DevOps Agent\",\"context\":\"## Introduction\\\\n\\\\nOrganizations that run generative AI workloads on [Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-bedrock.html) pay by the token. Retry loops that don\\'t back off, prompts that pass entire documents without truncation, and batch jobs without concurrency controls sometimes generate significant unexpected charges.\\\\n\\\\nThe challenge is timing. [AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html) updates hours after consumption occurs. By the time a cost anomaly appears in billing dashboards, the damage is done.\\\\n\\\\nHowever, Amazon Bedrock publishes **InputTokenCount** and **OutputTokenCount** metrics to [CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/WhatIsCloudWatch.html) within minutes of every model invocation. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock expands support for Service Quotas - AWS\",\"context\":\"Amazon Bedrock, a managed service for enterprise-grade access to high-performing foundation models from leading AI companies, now supports viewing inference quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint through AWS Service Quotas. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Sydney, Jakarta), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Stockholm), and South America (S\u00e3o Paulo)\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/5/amazon-bedrock-service-quotas/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock now supports observability of First Token Latency and Quota Consumption - AWS\",\"context\":\"Amazon Bedrock, a managed service for building AI applications using high-performance models from leading providers, has introduced two new CloudWatch metrics: TimeToFirstToken and EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage. EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage tracks quota consumption, including cache write tokens and output burndown multipliers, across all inference APIs (Converse, InvokeModel, ConverseStream, and InvokeModelWithResponseStream). This metric allows proactive alarm setting before quota limits, tracking quota consumption across models, and requesting quota increases before usage is rate-limited. Both metrics are available in all commercial Bedrock regions for models accessible via cross-region inference profiles and in-region inference, updated every minute for successfully completed requests, and incur no additional cost beyond model inference usage. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore (including the Harness managed agent loop). For SageMaker model discovery, customization, or endpoints, use aws-ai-ml.\\\\n\\\\nServices: bedrock, bedrock-runtime, bedrock-mantle, bedrock-agent, bedrock-agent-runtime, bedrock-agentcore-control, bedrock-agentcore\\\\nTasks: deploy, debug, optimize, design, migrate\\\\nPersona: developer, devops, architect\\\\nWorkload: generative-ai, rag, agents\",\"skill_name\":\"amazon-bedrock\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"writing-agentcore-policy\",\"skill_description\":\"Authors, validates and submits Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy statements (Cedar and Dogwood) for an AgentCore Gateway. Discovers the Gateway\\'s targets and tools, generates the Gateway\\'s Cedar schema, drafts permit/forbid, guardrail and temporal policies from access requirements or from a whole natural-language policy document (splitting it into rules, marking the rules that cannot be expressed, and repairing failing drafts in batches), checks them locally (syntax, schema, API limits, claim and guardrail pitfalls), and creates or updates them in a policy engine after explicit developer approval, reporting the final status and service findings. Use when a developer wants to write, translate, fix, validate or submit AgentCore Gateway policies, convert a policy document or a list of rules into policies, restrict which users or roles can call Gateway tools, add Bedrock guardrail or session-history (temporal) conditions, or resolve CreatePolicy/UpdatePolicy failures.\\\\n\\\\nServices: bedrock-agentcore-control, bedrock-agentcore\\\\nTasks: design, deploy, debug, secure\\\\nPersona: developer, security\\\\nWorkload: agents, generative-ai\",\"skill_name\":\"writing-agentcore-policy\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"aws-marketplace-metering\",\"skill_description\":\"Deploys, queries, and debugs AWS Marketplace usage-based (PAYG) metering \u2014 the pipeline (ResolveCustomer, BatchMeterUsage, EventBridge via SAM) and querying/debugging metering records, statuses, failures, discrepancies. Also SCOPES adjacent asks \u2014 flat-rate/SaaS-Subscription \\\\\"do I still meter\\\\\", CCP included-units + overage, contract term/annual renewal, forecasting future bills/usage \u2014 with the right answer or a one-line redirect. Use for any BatchMeterUsage/ResolveCustomer or SaaS usage-billing question.\\\\n\\\\nServices: aws-marketplace, marketplace-metering\\\\nTasks: deploy, integrate, query, debug, troubleshoot, analyze\\\\nPersona: developer\\\\nWorkload: saas\\\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"aws-marketplace-metering\"}]}}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_YSdM3FSLQKiJON2G8pWV4B", "content": "[{'text': '{\"012345678901_1\": []}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "b006ea22-ceeb-422a-ae1b-626f0531e4b2", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_GYUFuhI1ptnVTr5ukcCsDf", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\",\"content\":\"# Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle.region.api.aws` endpoint serves the OpenAI Responses API, the OpenAI Chat Completions API, and the Anthropic Messages API. Inference traffic to this endpoint is governed by a separate set of quotas from the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint.\\n\\nYou can view `bedrock-mantle` quotas in the Service Quotas console by selecting **Amazon Bedrock** as the service and searching for *Bedrock Mantle*. To request an increase to any of these quotas, see Requesting a quota increase.\\n\\n## Quota types\\n\\nInference on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint is governed by two per-model quotas:\\n\\nbedrock-mantle per-model quotas\\n\\n| Quota | Scope | Description |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Bedrock Mantle input tokens per minute for `${model}` | Per model, per Region | The maximum number of input tokens per minute that your account can submit to the model on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint. Shared across all APIs served by the endpoint for that model. |\\n| Bedrock Mantle output tokens per minute for `${model}` | Per model, per Region | The maximum number of output tokens per minute that the model can generate for your account on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint. Shared across all APIs served by the endpoint for that model. |\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nCached input tokens read through prompt caching do not count against the input-tokens-per-minute quota.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle` endpoint does not enforce requests-per-minute (RPM) quotas. Throttling is governed solely by the input and output token quotas described in this section.\\n\\n## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint.\\n\\n## View quota values\\n\\nQuota values vary by model, account, and AWS Region. To view the current default and\\napplied quota values for models available to your account, open the Service Quotas\\nconsole, select **Amazon Bedrock**, and search for\\n`bedrock-mantle endpoint`. Each quota name identifies the model and\\nwhether the value applies to input or output tokens per minute.\\n\\n## Supported Regions\\n\\n`bedrock-mantle` quotas are visible in Service Quotas in the same AWS Regions where the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint is available. For the full list of Regions and endpoint URLs, see Supported Regions and Endpoints.\\n\\n## Requesting a quota increase\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nA quota increase doesn't grant additional account-level access to a model. If you\\ncan't invoke a model after completing the activation requirements in Request access to models and verifying AWS Region\\nsupport, contact AWS\\nSales for additional access options.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle` quotas are visible in Service Quotas, but quota increase requests are not currently processed through the Service Quotas console. To request an increase, submit a request through the AWS Support limit increase form and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service. In your request, specify:\\n\\n* The endpoint (`bedrock-mantle`).\\n* The Region.\\n* The model.\\n* The quota name (input TPM or output TPM) and the value you are requesting.\\n\\nYou can request increases to input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute for the same model in a single support case. Approval depends on whether your existing usage justifies the increase, so include recent usage information from CloudWatch or the Service Quotas console with your request.\\n\\n## Differences from bedrock-runtime quotas\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle` quotas are independent from the `bedrock-runtime` quotas. Traffic to `bedrock-runtime.region.amazonaws.com` and traffic to `bedrock-mantle.region.api.aws` consume separate quota allocations, even when calling the same underlying model.\\n\\nCustom inference profile quotas, batch inference quotas, and Provisioned Throughput allocations apply only to the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint and are not exposed on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint.\",\"total_length\":5299,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":5299,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Read Bedrock mantle quotas documentation page"}

{"id": "8e71fa23-421b-4408-9fe9-d19c6e85aac9", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, that's very likely. The `mantle` in the usage type name points to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, so the Bedrock Mantle quotas are the ones that should apply to that traffic.

**What the docs say**
- The Bedrock Cost and Usage Report guide lists `*-mantle-input-tokens-*` as a separate usage type pattern from the plain `*-input-tokens` pattern. The plain pattern covers other routes, such as bedrock-runtime.
- The `standard` at the end of your usage type is the service tier.
- The `bedrock-mantle` endpoint serves the OpenAI Responses API, the OpenAI Chat Completions API and the Anthropic Messages API. Its quotas are separate from bedrock-runtime's. The two endpoints draw on separate quota allocations, even for the same model.
- The Bedrock docs describe the mantle usage type as a pattern but don't state the mapping to the endpoint in so many words. I'm basing the link on that naming and on how the docs separate the two endpoints.

**Which quota applies**
- The quota is "Bedrock Mantle input tokens per minute for Claude Sonnet 5". It's per model and per Region, so for your `USE1` usage it's the us-east-1 value. It isn't the runtime TPM quota.
- Mantle also has a separate output-tokens-per-minute quota.
- Mantle has no requests-per-minute quota, so throttling is based only on tokens.
- Cached input tokens read through prompt caching don't count against the input quota.
- Admission counts your input tokens plus the `max_tokens` value you set, or the model's maximum if you don't set one. Throttling can therefore happen earlier than your real input volume suggests. Any unused part of the reservation is returned after the response completes.
- Increases for mantle quotas aren't processed through the Service Quotas console. You request them with an AWS Support limit increase case for Amazon Bedrock. In the case, give the endpoint (`bedrock-mantle`), the Region, the model, the quota name and the value you want.

**What I couldn't confirm**
I listed the Bedrock quotas in Service Quotas for account 012345678901_1 in us-east-1. The query returned no entries with "Mantle" in the name. That doesn't prove the quota is missing. It could be a naming difference in my filter or a quota that isn't exposed for this model yet. Search for "Bedrock Mantle" in the Service Quotas console to see your current value.

To confirm the traffic path, check what your application calls. A base URL like `bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws` means mantle. A call through `bedrock-runtime`, using Converse or InvokeModel, would be billed under the runtime usage types instead.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
